resources.string: When you call or text an emergency number, your phone can send its location straight to the emergency service. This is called Advanced Mobile Location (AML) and it can help them get to you faster.
Send my location in an emergency
Emergency services on your current network (%1$s) accept AML.
AML is not set up for the network you are on right now, so no location would be sent from here.
You are not connected to a mobile network right now.
CipherAML is missing permissions it needs (%1$s), so it may not be able to send your location. Tap here to fix it.

Your location is only sent during an emergency call or emergency SMS, only to the emergency service of the country you are in, and only if that country supports AML. For that moment GPS and Wi-Fi location are used even if you normally keep location off. Nothing is sent to CipherOS or anyone else, and nothing is saved on your phone.
Emergency calls always go through, whether this is on or off.
